summary: Through the early 1920s the Board was drawing set-back lines down this neighbourhood's avenues — thirty feet on Ninth, fifteen on Funston, ten on Nineteenth — fixing how far back from the street a house was allowed to stand, one avenue at a time. In 1924 the Sunset Community Improvement Club protested against a stable on Fourteenth Avenue between Lincoln and Irving. The year before, the city had been working out where the new municipal railway line would let passengers change onto the Market Street Railway: Twentieth and Judah, Ninth and Judah, Stanyan and Carl.

summary_sources.for: thirty feet back on Ninth Avenue
summary_sources.t: Along the easterly side of Ninth avenue between Lawton and Moraga streets, which said set-back line shall be thirty feet distant from and parallel with the line of Ninth avenue.
Along both sides of Nineteenth avenue between Noriega street and Ortega street, which said set-back line shall be ten feet distant from and parallel with the line of Nineteenth avenue.

Along the westerly side of Funston avenue, commencing at Kirkham street and running thence northerly 225 feet, said set-back line to be 15 feet; thence northerly 75 feet, said set-back line to be 3.5 feet…
Protest from the Sunset Community Improvement club, against the maintenance of a stable on Fourteenth avenue between Lincoln and Irving streets.

On the completion of the construction of the line it will require transfer arrangements with the Market Street Railway Company at Twentieth avenue and Judah street, Ninth avenue and Judah street, and Stanyan street and Carl street…
